title: Ephemeral Runners

content.intro: This lesson focuses on ephemeral runners. Ephemeral runners are disposed after a job so one workload does not leave residual state or credentials for the next job. Use the example to predict the workflow result, then verify the behavior in a safe test repository or by static review.
content.why_it_matters: Ephemeral Runners matters because it affects correctness, security, maintainability, or operating cost. Ephemeral runners are disposed after a job so one workload does not leave residual state or credentials for the next job. Self-hosted runners provide control but widen the operational responsibility. Restrict access, isolate trust levels, patch images, remove residual state, and monitor fleet health.

jobs:
  internal-check:
    runs-on: [self-hosted, linux, x64]
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - run: echo "Route only trusted workloads to this runner group"

content.expected_output: The expected result is the behavior described here: Ephemeral runners are disposed after a job so one workload does not leave residual state or credentials for the next job. The real result depends on the repository, selected ref, configured permissions, and runner availability.
troubleshooting: If a workflow never starts, verify the workflow is under `.github/workflows/`, the event and filters match, and repository/organization Actions policy allows it.
If a step fails, inspect the first failed step, exit code, stderr, installed tool versions, permissions, and runner/network state before retrying.
If a job is skipped or data is missing, inspect `if`, `needs`, outputs, artifact names/paths, and cache keys; jobs do not automatically share filesystems.
common_mistakes: Assuming YAML parsing proves the workflow runs correctly or matches the intended trigger.
Granting broad token permissions, printing environment values, or exposing a secret to untrusted code.
Using a placeholder command as evidence of a real build, test, deployment, or security scan.
